scale.note: 10^(-2.725) m = 0.001883 m, reported in the slot brief as 1.9 mm

evolutionary_history.what_changes: At 1.883 mm the Holocene plains zebra selects a fastest Turing mode (vertical flank stripes). The Pleistocene predecessor Equus scotti is the equal-diffusion control: the onset numerator changes sign and no wavelength is selected.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.pde: du/dt = Du lap(u) + gamma f; dv/dt = div(Dv grad v) + gamma g
equations.onset_wavenumber: k_c^2 = gamma (Dv,x f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv,x) for ky = 0
equations.fast_wavenumber: k_fast = argmax_k Re sigma(k, ky=0), with sigma from the gamma-scaled Jacobian
equations.wavelength: lambda = 2 pi / k_fast, pinned to 0.001883 m at gamma = 1.15

boundary_conditions: periodic flank patch; inhibitor diffusion anisotropic, faster along the anteroposterior axis so the selected wavevector is longitudinal and stripes stand perpendicular to the dorsal line (Bard 1977)

empirical_claims.bard_1977_timing: third embryonic week for plains zebra (E. burchelli), stripes perpendicular to the dorsal line
empirical_claims.note: The 2.03 mm figure is the periodic-domain FFT of the nonlinear field (nearest integer mode). It is not a second empirical caliper measurement.

specimen.creator: Yathin S Krishnappa
specimen.role: Adult flank pattern class. Not a scale bar for the 1.883 mm fetal wavelength.
